Argentina.why: Argentina have won six of their seven World Cup penalty shootouts, more than any other nation.

perk.name: Shootout nerve
perk.blurb: Penalty takers and the keeper stay calm in a shootout.

Australia.why: 2006 v Japan: 0-1 down until the 84th minute, won 3-1 with three goals in the last eight minutes (Cahill twice, Aloisi).

perk.name: Late surge
perk.blurb: Forwards come alive in the last ten minutes when level or behind, and there is extra injury time.

Belgium.why: 2018 round of 16 v Japan: 0-2 down, won 3-2 with a counter-attack in the 94th minute.

perk.name: Counter-punch
perk.blurb: After repelling an attack they hit back on the counter more often.

Brazil.why: Five World Cups and a name for flair. The wobble is the 7-1 semi-final defeat to Germany in 2014.

perk.name: Jogo bonito
perk.blurb: Forwards get a small flair bonus.

quirk.name: Mineirazo
quirk.blurb: Two or more goals behind and the whole team wobbles.

Cameroon.why: 1990: beat holders Argentina 1-0 in the opener after two Cameroon red cards, and became the first African side in a World Cup quarter-final.

perk.name: Indomitable
perk.blurb: Strong in the tackle and in the air.

Colombia.why: 2014: 12 goals in five matches, with James Rodriguez winning the Golden Boot.

perk.name: Free-scoring
perk.blurb: Forwards get a small finishing bonus.

Croatia.why: Won all four of their World Cup shootouts (Denmark, Russia, Japan, Brazil), and in 2018 played extra time in three knockout games in a row.

perk.name: Never say die
perk.blurb: Penalty takers and the keeper stay calm in a shootout, and legs hold up in extra time.

Denmark.why: The nickname dates from 1986, when they beat Uruguay 6-1 and won all three group games.

perk.name: Danish Dynamite
perk.blurb: Explosive starts: more chances in the first twenty minutes.

England.why: In 2018 England scored 9 of their 12 goals from set pieces, a World Cup record.

perk.name: Set-piece threat
perk.blurb: More goals from headers and set plays.

France.why: 2022 final: 0-2 down to Argentina, level at 2-2 within two minutes of Mbappe scoring in the 80th.

perk.name: Les Bleus never quit
perk.blurb: Forwards come alive in the last ten minutes when level or behind, and there is extra injury time.

Germany.why: Won their first four World Cup shootouts (1982, 1986, 1990, 2006). They lost their first in 2026, to Paraguay.

perk.name: Nervenstaerke
perk.blurb: Penalty takers and the keeper stay calm in a shootout.

Ireland.why: 2002 v Germany: Robbie Keane equalised in the 92nd minute to rescue a 1-1 draw.

perk.name: Boys in Green
perk.blurb: Forwards come alive in the last ten minutes when level or behind, and there is extra injury time.

Italy.why: 2006 winners conceded two goals all tournament (an own goal and a penalty). But Italy lost their first three World Cup shootouts (1990, 1994, 1998).

perk.name: Catenaccio
perk.blurb: Opponents create fewer chances.

quirk.name: Shootout jitters
quirk.blurb: Penalty takers are less composed in a shootout.

Japan.why: 2022: beat Germany and then Spain 2-1, both from a goal down at half-time.

perk.name: Samurai spirit
perk.blurb: Behind at half-time, they change their approach and attack the weakest line.

Morocco.why: 2022: conceded one goal in the tournament before the semi-final, an own goal against Canada.

perk.name: Atlas wall
perk.blurb: Opponents create fewer chances.

Netherlands.why: Positional interchange was the Michels and Cruyff idea of 1974. They have also lost three finals (1974, 1978, 2010).

perk.name: Total Football
perk.blurb: Players lose almost nothing when moved out of position.

quirk.name: Final jinx
quirk.blurb: A small dip in a World Cup final.

Nigeria.why: Nickname perk: Eagles win the high ball.

perk.name: Super Eagles
perk.blurb: They fly: more goals from headers.

Norway.why: Egil Olsen's direct style took Norway to 1998, where they beat Brazil 2-1.

perk.name: Route one
perk.blurb: Direct football: more crosses and high balls, and more headed goals.

Saudi Arabia.why: 2022: beat Argentina 2-1 on their way to being the biggest upset of the tournament.

perk.name: Giant-killers
perk.blurb: A rating boost against stronger opponents.

Scotland.why: 1978: beat the Netherlands 3-2, the eventual finalists.

perk.name: Tartan Army
perk.blurb: A rating boost against stronger opponents.

South Korea.why: 2002: beat Italy 2-1 with a golden goal in extra time, then Spain on penalties after a 0-0 extra time.

perk.name: Taegeuk fitness
perk.blurb: Legs hold up in extra time while opponents tire.

Spain.why: 2010 winners scored eight goals in seven games, the fewest by any champion.

perk.name: Tiki-taka
perk.blurb: Midfield controls the ball and is stronger.

quirk.name: 1-0 specialists
quirk.blurb: Low-scoring games: fewer chances at both ends.

Switzerland.why: 2006: first team ever out of a World Cup without conceding a goal in normal play, beaten 3-0 on penalties by Ukraine without scoring one.

perk.name: Swiss lock
perk.blurb: Opponents create fewer chances.

quirk.name: Shootout jitters
quirk.blurb: Penalty takers are less composed in a shootout.

Uruguay.why: Nickname perk: garra charrua, the fighting spirit of La Celeste.

perk.name: Garra Charrua
perk.blurb: Work rate up: they do not get out-fought.
